<reason>CON won a competitive debate by isolating the motion's distinctive increment—legal-identity attachment, not mere liveness—and weighing irreversible exclusion and retention risk against only a delay to professional fraud. PRO was rhetorically sharp on “maybe-people,” but kept shrinking the proposal (no badge, one-time attest) until it either duplicated tools CON already accepted or recreated the dossier CON attacked. The clipped CON rebuttal is a real execution cost, yet the live comparison still favored CON.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON's Rebuttal 2 fork: ban-persistence needs a retained identifier, so PRO cannot claim both “no dossier” and a unique anti-fiction increment over liveness checks.</best_rebuttal>
